Is Generac Holdings a Bargain on Cash Flow?

The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model here focuses on what Generac Holdings can return to shareholders in future free cash. Latest twelve month free cash flow sits at about $386.3m, and the projections used in this 2 Stage Free Cash Flow to Equity approach assume growing cash generation out toward 2030 rather than a shrinking stream.

Those higher future cash flow estimates, when discounted back, imply an intrinsic worth that the model suggests is substantially above the current US$189.23 share price. Because the long term backup power deal with Amazon points to sizeable shipments in 2027 and 2028, the market may still be debating how much of that potential is already reflected in the cash flow path used in the DCF. Amazon.com (AMZN) is back in the spotlight as investors watch for its third quarter 2026 earnings on October 29, with attention squarely on AWS, AI spending and overall profitability.

Recent trading reflects that tension between enthusiasm and scrutiny. Amazon.com's share price is up 9.9% over the past 90 days but down 5.2% over the last week, while the 3-year total shareholder return of 87.2% shows longer term momentum that earnings, AI investment headlines and Fed rate expectations continue to test.

After a sharp 3 year climb and a choppy recent week, Amazon.com now asks a simple question of investors: Does the AI capex and earnings profile still set up as a favourable risk reward from here as you look at valuation next?

Most Popular Narrative: 48% Undervalued

On the numbers, the narrative fair value for Amazon.com sits at $475.09 per share against a last close of $249.09, which frames a wide valuation gap that investors now weigh against AI capex, AWS trends and cash generation.

Amazon is a company of two sides: a high tech, high margin side, comprising its AWS, Advertising and subscription services segments, and its more traditionally known low margin, high volume stores and third-party seller segments.

These two sides form a cohesive whole. The Amazon online store motivates customers to purchase subscriptions and hosts its advertising. AWS underpins the functioning of the online store, but is also easy to integrate with for Amazon's many third-party sellers, encouraging adoption.

Prediction: This Artificial Intelligence (AI) Memory Stock Will Go Parabolic on Oct. 30
Adam Spatacco, The Motley Fool

MU
GOOG
NVDA

As technology companies race to build data centers, demand for the memory chips that make artificial intelligence (AI) computing possible has skyrocketed. One of the leading manufacturers of memory chips for AI hyperscalers is Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU).

So far this year, Micron stock has soared 225% -- making it the third-highest performer in the Nasdaq-100. Nevertheless, Micron's shares have experienced considerable volatility over the last couple of months and trade about 24% below their all-time high.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

I think this disconnect is about to reverse. On Oct. 28 and 29, Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL) (NASDAQ: GOOG) and Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) are scheduled to report quarterly earnings. While investors will undoubtedly focus on their respective AI-related capital expenditures (capex), I think another topic could emerge as a major discussion point: the global memory shortage. If my prediction is accurate, Micron could begin to rally just in time for Halloween.

Amazon already warned investors about rising memory costs

For most of the AI revolution, investors primarily associated infrastructure with graphics processing units (GPUs) designed by Nvidia and application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) designed by Broadcom. However, GPUs and custom silicon cannot operate efficiently without sufficient memory. Micron manufactures dynamic random access memory (DRAM) and high bandwidth memory (HBM), both of which are critical components of the AI chip stack.

Interestingly, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy already highlighted the growing importance of memory during the company's last earnings call. Jassy explained that Amazon planned to increase its 2026 capex budget to $220 billion -- up from its previous forecast of $200 billion -- specifically because of higher memory costs.

Meanwhile, Alphabet raised its 2026 capex forecast to $195 billion to $205 billion during its second-quarter earnings call. Management attributed the increase to accelerating infrastructure investments and capacity supply constraints. Although Alphabet did not explicitly identify memory as the culprit, its comments reinforce the underlying idea that demand for AI compute is insatiable.

As both companies prepare to report earnings this week, investors should pay close attention to any additional commentary surrounding memory availability, pricing, and infrastructure spending.

Alphabet's GOOGL third-quarter 2026 results, scheduled to be released on Oct. 28, are expected to have benefited from solid momentum in Search and Cloud businesses. The momentum in Search is expected to have driven advertising revenues in the to-be-reported quarter. The Cloud business is riding on strong demand for AI infrastructure and an expanding clientele.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Google's advertising revenues is currently pegged at $83.523 billion, suggesting 12.6% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter. The consensus mark for Google Cloud revenues is currently pegged at $29.16 billion, indicating 92.3% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

Alphabet has an impressive earnings surprise history. GOOGL's earnings outpaced the Zacks Consensus Estimate in all the trailing four quarters, the average surprise being 86.65%.

GOOGL's AI Push Aids Search & Cloud Businesses

GOOGL's Search business is benefiting from AI infusion. Alphabet is leading the search domain with 89.94% market share, followed by Microsoft's MSFT Bing, with 5.29% share, Yahoo!'s 1.36%, Yandex's 1.3%, DuckDuckGo's 0.74% and Baidu's 0.44%, per the latest data from StatCounter.

Google Search & Other revenues are likely to have benefited from growing user engagement with AI-powered search experiences, including AI Overviews and AI Mode. The integration of these capabilities into a seamless search experience is expected to have increased query volumes and created additional advertising opportunities. AI Mode surpassed 1 billion monthly active users in the second quarter, with management highlighting incremental growth in overall search queries.

Improving advertising relevance through Gemini-powered query understanding, AI Max and Performance Max are expected to have supported monetization. AI Max had already attracted 500,000 advertisers, while AI-powered campaigns generated an average of 15% more conversions or conversion value on Search at a similar return on advertising spend. Continued demand from retail and financial services advertisers, which were major contributors to second-quarter growth, is likely to have supported Search revenues in the to-be-reported quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Search and other revenues is currently pegged at $65 billion, suggesting 15% growth over the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

Meanwhile, Google Cloud is expected to have remained a major growth engine in the to-be-reported quarter. Google Cloud has solidified its position as the third-largest provider in the highly competitive cloud infrastructure market against the likes of Microsoft Azure and Amazon's AMZN Amazon Web Services. According to Synergy Research Group data, Google Cloud, along with Microsoft, is gaining market share, while Amazon continues to lead with a 28% market share in the second quarter of 2026. Alphabet and Microsoft had 15% and 20% market share, respectively.

Google Cloud is expected to have benefited from robust enterprise demand for AI infrastructure, accelerated adoption of Gemini Enterprise and growing consumption of Google Cloud Platform services. Demand for Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), NVIDIA GPUs and AI inference capabilities is likely to have supported infrastructure revenues, while increasing adoption of BigQuery, cybersecurity solutions and Google Workspace is expected to have strengthened cloud applications and platform revenues. Cloud's expanding enterprise customer base and rising consumption among existing customers are additional positives.

Strategic Inflection and Premium Growth Execution

Our analysts just identified a stock with the potential to be the next Nvidia. Tell us how you invest and we'll show you why it's our #1 pick. Tap here.

Management declared a strategic inflection point in the U.S. Domestic segment, where revenue per piece growth outpaced cost per piece for the second consecutive quarter, driving a 60 basis point margin expansion.

Performance was attributed to a deliberate shift toward high-value 'premium' volume, with SMB and enterprise average daily volume increasing 1.8% while lower-margin Amazon volume was intentionally reduced.

The company implemented a new global operating model to standardize critical processes across geographies, aiming to accelerate synergies between Small Package, Healthcare, and Logistics businesses.

Operational efficiency is being driven by the transition from a 'scanning' to a 'sensing' network, utilizing RFID technology to eliminate billions of manual scans and improve package visibility.

International profit returned to growth for the first time in six quarters, fueled by strong demand in China-to-U.S. and Asia-to-Asia trade lanes despite broader geopolitical tensions.

The Supply Chain Solutions segment leveraged demand from high-tech and healthcare sectors to grow revenue, specifically highlighting the $15 billion logistics opportunity presented by global data center expansion.

Raised Outlook and Peak Season Readiness

Full-year 2026 guidance was raised to approximately $92.6 billion in revenue and $8.75 billion in operating profit, reflecting confidence in the momentum of premium volume growth.

Fourth-quarter planning assumes a 25% sequential volume surge for the peak holiday season, with 80% of this surge driven by a concentrated group of approximately 100 large customers.

Management expects nearly 70% of peak volume to flow through automated processes, allowing the company to handle holiday demand with fewer vehicle rentals and aircraft leases than in previous years.

The Digital Access Program (DAP) is projected to continue its shift toward premium mix, with air services and ground commercial already representing nearly 30% of total DAP volume.

Free cash flow is expected to reach approximately $6.1 billion for the full year, supported by business outperformance and a strategic pension contribution made using UPS bonds rather than cash.

Structural Adjustments and Transformation Costs

GAAP results included a $279 million net charge, primarily comprised of $130 million in transformation strategy costs and a $182 million goodwill impairment in Supply Chain Solutions.

The Driver Choice Program concluded with approximately 1,500 participants exiting the company, a structural labor adjustment that required $1.4 billion in cash payments during 2026.

Management highlighted the successful issuance of $1.3 billion in debt to refinance maturities and strengthen the pension plan's funded status through a $450 million bond contribution.

A $33 million gain from the sale of MD-11 assets partially offset transformation charges, reflecting ongoing efforts to modernize the global air fleet.

When Should You Buy DoorDash Stock?

Shares of DoorDash (DASH) have lost 33.8% over the past twelve months, a period when the S&P 500 returned 15.3%. The stock now sits 36.7% below its highest close of the past year, even though the company posted sales growth in each of its last four reported quarters. Has the fall made DoorDash cheap, or is buying now still too early?

DoorDash Now Costs About Half As Much On Sales

A lower share price and a year of 33.6% sales growth have combined to make DoorDash cheaper on a sales basis than it has usually been. At the end of September, the shares traded at 5.0 times twelve-month sales. That multiple is about half the 9.7 times recorded a year earlier, and the stock had traded lower at only 9 of the 24 quarter ends since 2020.

Underlying business operations did not weaken over the twelve months ending in June. During that period, DoorDash reported an operating margin of 4.8%, slightly above the 4.6% recorded a year earlier. The June quarter itself stands as the exception, producing a 3.5% operating margin compared to 5.0% a year earlier.

The stock looks significantly more expensive on profit than on cash. At the October 26 close, DoorDash traded at 87.0 times earnings against 25.9 times operating cash flow. In other words, the company's operations bring in far more cash than it reports as profit.

How Much Growth Are DoorDash Buyers Paying For?

Forecasts for the next report indicate growth will remain near the 35.6% pace DoorDash reported for the June quarter, rather than accelerating. Analysts expect revenue of $4.66 billion for the third quarter of 2026, about 35% more than a year earlier. The company describes this growth as broad. In its release for the June quarter, DoorDash said its marketplaces, membership programs, and monthly active users all grew strongly in the first half of 2026 against a year earlier.

What Could Buying DoorDash Before November Cost You?

Buying before November means accepting a reaction to results that has historically moved in both directions. DoorDash will report its third-quarter 2026 results in November 2026. Over the two trading days following each of its last six reports, the stock rose three times and fell three times. The largest move was a 14.2% fall after the November 2025 report, while the most recent was a 4.3% gain after the August 2026 report.

A wider sell-off represents the other cost of buying early. During the 2025 tariff shock, DoorDash fell 23.0% from peak to low, compared to 19.0% for the S&P 500. Additionally, news reports on October 26 said DoorDash was in advanced talks to acquire Instacart. Those reports said a deal could be completed as soon as this week, before the November report. Neither company has confirmed the talks, and the test below covers only the November results, not the deal.
